feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(\pm a,0).$ From the graph, we have that $(3,0)$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=3.$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}x,$ and so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{b}{a} & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3} \\ \frac{b}{3} & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3} \\ b & =\sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
